keyFindings.description: After a failure past the send (role claim or controller-topic subscribe), the warning says /legion-claim-controller 'sends the start message once the claim succeeds', but startMessageSent blocks any second send; the start turn ran while the legion tool refused (controllerSessionID unset) and is never re-run. legion.test.ts:2838 pins the false text and :2856 asserts the retry sends nothing. The PR widened this: the send moved before claimEnvoyRole.

startupTurn is not cleared in the follow-up case: the operator's run already fired agent_start before markStartupTurnSent, and Oh My Pi consumes a followUp inside the same run (agent-loop.ts:648 agent_start once per run, :1823-1827 follow-ups drained in-run; agent-session.ts:9426 followUp only queues). The mark stays set after the start turn ran, contrary to pi-legion AGENTS.md:388-390, startup-turn.ts:3-5 and interface.ts:45-46. A /new during the claim marks the old session id. This mark is the spec's deliverable for pi-envoy.

No `## Contract change census`, though the PR adds a refusal (non-terminal stdin, controller.go:126), bumps the daemon API contract 40->41 (skewed CLI/plugin refused) and the plugin interface 3->4 (pi-envoy/pi-legion pair).

startupTurn's type admits a marked-but-unsent state nothing produces; pi-shared AGENTS.md:46 ('undefined until sent') and interface.ts:43 ('/legion-controller-start sets both', but any claim that sends does) describe the earlier design. Fix before interface 4 ships, since a later shape change needs another lockstep bump.

The start turn now starts before claimEnvoyRole and the subscription; controllerSessionID/mintControllerGrant are set only after them (:261-263), so a slow listener makes the start procedure's first legion call refused.
A claim that hangs (daemon-client sets no timeout) now silently blocks /legion-claim-controller and a re-run of the command; tell the operator it waits for the claim in flight.
console.error now runs while the TUI is up (no console interception in the pinned Oh My Pi); use the logger.

Still says a LEGION_CONTROLLER=1 session claims at startup as the launched controller; the operator-launched controller now claims from /legion-controller-start (also the claude-envoy generated copy).
